title.narrative: Sustainable Use of Natural Resources for Environment and Econ. Dev.-SUNREED
Sustainable Use of Natural Resources for Environment and Econ. Dev.-SUNREED

description.narrative:
Det övergripande målet med konceptförslaget "Hållbar användning av naturresurser för miljö och ekonomisk utveckling" är att öka en hållbar användning av privata skogsresurser och utveckling av värdekedjan för förnybar energi baserad på träbiomassa (fjärrvärmesystem) som kommer att generera en större mängd skogsvaror och inkomstmöjligheter för hushåll på landsbygden. Målet för projektförslagen kommer att uppnås genom följande två resultat: Resultat 1: Privata skogsägare har ökat värdet och hållbarheten i skogsståndens ekosystem. Resultat 2: Värdekedjornas aktörer har ökat produktionen, bearbetningen och slutanvändningen av träbiomassa.
Genomförandepartner är CNVP Foundation. Projektet kommer att inriktas på att ta itu med de privata skogsägarnas centrala begränsningar och ge stöd till dem när det gäller att samla in bevis och förespråka politiska och rättsliga förändringar med offentliga institutioner till förmån för privat skogsbruk.

The overall objective of the concept proposal “Sustainable Use of Natural Resources for Environment and Economic Development, shortly SUNREED” is to increase the sustainable use of private forest resources and value chain development on renewable energy based on wood biomass (district heating system) that will generate a higher volume of forest goods and income opportunities to rural households. The project proposals goal will be achieved through the following two outcomes: Outcome 1: Private forest owners have increased value and sustainability of the forest stand ecosystems. Outcome 2: Value chains actors have increased wood biomass production, processing and final use.
The implementing partner is CNVP Foundation. The project will be focused on addressing key constraint faced by the private forest owners and provide support to them in collecting evidence and advocating for policy and legal changes with public institutions in favor of private forestry.

title.narrative: SUSTAINABLE USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES FOR ENVIRONMENT AND ECON. DEV.SUNREED
SUSTAINABLE USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES FOR ENVIRONMENT AND ECON. DEV.SUNREED

description.narrative:
In 2024, SUNREED continued to strengthen sustainable forestry and rural livelihoods in Kosovo by improving forest management, building market links for non-wood forest products (NWFPs) and medicinal/aromatic plants (MAPs), and advancing the use of sustainably sourced biomass.
What changed in 2024:
Better-managed private forests. 300 private forest owners (PFOs) now have approved forest management plans covering over 1,800 hectares, enabling planned thinning and improved stewardship.
Income opportunities from residues. The first biomass collection point in eastern Kosovo (Viti) became operational, allowing PFOs to sell low value wood residues that were previously unused.
Real market transactions. 60 PFOs sold a combined 13,200 m of wood biomass to established buyers, confirming supply chain functionality between forest owners and processors.
Advisory services for forest owners. The National Association of Private Forest Owners (NAPFO) piloted advisory and training services on safe, sustainable harvesting and compliance an important first for service delivery to PFOs.
Women and youth participation. Three new Women & Youth Producer Groups linked 260 collectors (132 women) to processors, with participants reporting at least 10% higher incomes through improved market access.
Quality and export readiness in MAPs. 10 advisors were trained and certified in organic MAP cultivation and sustainable wild collection, supporting higher standards and market access.
Long-term biomass supply. Partners established 4 hectares of fast-growing tree plantations and a 0.2hectare nursery to secure future sustainable feedstock.
Heating preparedness in schools. Three feasibility studies for biomass heating were completed; thinning produced 75 m of biomass used to help heat primary schools in Hani i Elezit Municipality.
Policy groundwork. A national biomass roadmap and a carbon market roadmap were finalized and discussed with municipalities and stakeholders (including three municipal MoU's and national policy events)
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
